saw_lines: People buy one wallet, carry it daily, and switch only when a feature like tracking makes the old one feel outdated.
So the sale is won in the first line, where a buyer decides if a tracking feature is worth switching for.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 31 Oct 2026
points: Your site shows 50,000+ reviews, yet only 3 of 28 ads carry a proof number. Buyers check reviews first, so the number must show early. Put 46567 reviews on every creative and open two ads with a review quote.

The offer lands after 78% of the copy, so most viewers miss it. Your site runs 33% off the Ekster Wallet Bundle, yet 0 of 28 ads mention a bundle. Open every ad with that bundle in its first two lines.

One exact copy runs in 9 of 28 ads, so the same message reaches the same viewers repeatedly. Keep the body copy, rewrite the first line and swap the creative in those 9 ads. Give each version its own visual.

9 of 28 copy ads open on the same Steven Bartlett line. Only 1 ad mentions price, so buyers rarely hear it. Test two new openers against it, one on price and one on the Tracker Card, never lose your gear.

ads_1: Price and tracker card openers, tested against the Steven Bartlett hook
